keyFindings.description: warnOrErrorRecords' comment (lines 166-168) says a client started without a name of its own still passes the filter; it does not: such a client is named "envoy" (parseConnectOptions, nats.go:64), so every WARN and ERROR record it logs is dropped by line 189 and the drain assertion silently checks nothing. The helper must refuse a client under test that is not named t.Name() (fail when no captured record names it, or take the name from the caller next to WithName), and the comment must say so.

The table test does not pin 'any other refusal is returned at once': a regression that settles every refusal from the stream passes the 'refused otherwise' row because the stream does not hold the update there. Count the fake's StreamInfo reads per row, add a row for another refusal while the stream holds the update (want the refusal, 1 send, 0 reads), write the 'refused four times' row in terms of overlapSends, and have the fake's landed update not hard-code Replicas = 3.

updateStream's loop (lines 528-540) carries the unanswered rule only as '!overlap ||' in its third exit. A loop over overlapSends sends that breaks on any answer but 10065, then one unanswered-and-settled check after it, gives the same sends and reads in every case (checked case by case: 5 refusals, unanswered, overlap then unanswered, other refusal, success) without the flag, the counter and the double negatives.
